subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should OpenClaw add user-prompt replacement to `before_prompt_build` with legacy `before_agent_start` compatibility, or should prompt rewriting be handled only by a broader `llm_input` interception API?
rationale: This is a new plugin API and security boundary that lets enabled plugins rewrite model-bound user input, so automation should not choose the hook layer, precedence, or audit behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add prompt-build replacement
options.body: Add a documented replacement field to `before_prompt_build`, carry it through legacy `before_agent_start`, enforce `allowPromptInjection`, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

options.title: Use broader LLM interception
options.body: Defer this issue to an `llm_input`-style modifying hook if maintainers want rewriting at the provider-boundary rather than the prompt-build boundary.

options.title: Reject replacement
options.body: Keep prompt hooks additive-only and direct oversized-prompt mitigation to context-engine/provider-boundary mechanisms instead.

recommendation.title: Add prompt-build replacement
recommendation.body: Add a documented replacement field to `before_prompt_build`, carry it through legacy `before_agent_start`, enforce `allowPromptInjection`, and cover embedded, CLI, and harness runners.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent merged history on Codex prompt hook parity and shared hook contract extraction, which are central to the cross-runner API choice.
